findings.title: Retry cleanup deletes reminders for every delivery method
findings.body: The `retryCount > 1` arm of this `OR` is not constrained to `WorkflowMethods.SMS` (or to unscheduled reminders). Consequently, any WorkflowReminder record of another method, such as email or WhatsApp, with a retryCount above one will be permanently deleted by the SMS cron. Retry cleanup must be scoped to SMS reminders so this endpoint cannot delete unrelated workflow delivery records.

findings.title: Reminders with no usable recipient or message never consume retries
findings.body: RetryCount is only incremented inside the `message?.length && sendTo` branch. An SMS attendee reminder without `booking.smsReminderNumber`, an SMS-number workflow with no `sendTo`, or a reminder whose generated message is empty is silently skipped and remains `scheduled: false` with retryCount 0. The cron will select it on every run until its scheduled date, which leaves a common class of unsendable SMS reminders with the behavior this change is intended to stop.

findings.title: Retry increments can be lost between concurrent cron invocations
findings.body: The retry value is read in `findMany` and later written as `reminder.retryCount + 1`, rather than incremented atomically or guarded by the previously read value. If two overlapping cron requests process the same unscheduled reminder, both can read 0 and both write 1 after failures. The reminder then receives additional scheduling attempts beyond the intended two-failure limit (and concurrent successful calls can also schedule duplicate SMS messages). Use an atomic increment together with a claim/conditional update of the reminder before scheduling.
